environment.purpose: Persistent shared development for synthetic identities, rows, and files only
environment.addressPolicy: Use only the provider-managed App Platform default address. Custom domains are outside Phase 14.

maintenanceSequence: Enable App Platform maintenance mode before the first deploy or any later incompatible release.
Create or update only the approved project assignments, database cluster, private bucket, application, and scoped identities.
Run database-migrate once and require the exact Alembic head before starting compatible services.
Start Keycloak, remove bootstrap access, require administrator MFA, and verify issuer and signing-key identity.
Start API and web, then workers with release processing disabled until their health and secret routes pass.
Prove backups, safe logs, worker claims, restart persistence, and the synthetic browser journeys.
Record the exact promotion approval, enable worker processing, then disable maintenance mode.

artifactIdentity.deploymentRule: Automatic branch deployment is disabled. A release manifest must bind every deployed artifact and configuration digest to one reviewed commit.

healthRules.rule: Exit zero, one head at e8a1c3f5b7d9, and a repeat run reports no pending migration.
GET /health returns HTTP 200 with status ok and database ok within five seconds.
GET /management/health/ready on internal port 9000 returns HTTP 200, then issuer discovery and JWKS succeed through /auth.
GET / returns HTTP 200 and the delivered bytes match the release manifest.
The scheduled run exits zero, records its business date and scope, and cannot overlap the same scope.
The provider reports one active worker and a sanitized heartbeat or completed claim is no older than two minutes.
The provider reports one active worker and a sanitized heartbeat or completed claim is no older than two minutes.

workerConcurrency.expiryConcurrency: One scheduled invocation at a time, plus one database advisory lock per company, branch scope, and business date.

secretCustody.runtime: DigitalOcean App Platform encrypted runtime settings, routed only to the owning component.
secretCustody.bootstrap: Short-lived values entered outside Git and removed or revoked after setup.
secretCustody.terraform: Encrypted owner-controlled state outside the repository; no plan, state, backup, token, password, private key, or signed URL enters Git.
secretCustody.operator: The project owner and a named backup custodian hold MFA and break-glass material in an owner-approved password manager.
secretCustody.evidence: Only names, identifiers, safe key suffixes, timestamps, and digests may be recorded.

operatorAccess.rule: 14G must map every role to a named person, a least-privilege account, MFA status, and a backup before apply. One person may hold several roles, but release approval and execution must be recorded separately.
operatorAccess.console: Routine operation uses provider and application controls. Direct database, container, or Keycloak administrator access is break-glass only and time bounded.

backupClasses.content: Managed PostgreSQL backups and point-in-time recovery for both databases
backupClasses.minimum: Provider schedule and retention verified at 14G

backupClasses.minimum: Seven daily copies and four weekly copies

backupClasses.content: Private object versions plus count, byte, key, and digest manifests
backupClasses.minimum: Versioning enabled and deleted versions retained for 30 days

backupClasses.content: Release manifest, app spec, configuration names, image and frontend digests, and schema head
backupClasses.minimum: Current and prior compatible release for at least 90 days

recoveryOrder: Put the shared app in maintenance mode and stop worker processing without deleting data.
Create exact isolated recovery targets and record their identifiers.
Restore both PostgreSQL databases from the matching backup class.
Restore private object versions and verify counts, bytes, keys, and digests.
Deploy the matching Keycloak artifact and verify signing-key continuity before login tests.
Deploy the matching API and frontend artifacts with writes and workers disabled.
Verify the schema head, identities, authorization, files, reconciliation state, and synthetic browser journeys.
Enable isolated writes only for the rehearsal, retain sanitized evidence, then delete only the named recovery targets.
monitoringSignals: API availability, latency, and error rate
Keycloak readiness, login failures, and signing-key changes
PostgreSQL capacity, connections, locks, and backup state
private object growth, errors, and versioning state
scanner and reconciler queue age, attempts, leases, and terminal failures
promotionEvidence: named operational owners and MFA state
synthetic administrator, manager, and employee journeys
deploymentRollbackOrder: Stop expiry, scanner, and reconciliation processing.
Select the prior reviewed artifact set that is compatible with the current schema.
Preserve the current databases, private objects, logs, and incident evidence. Never downgrade the schema automatically.
Redeploy Keycloak, API, web, scanner, reconciler, and expiry from the selected release manifest.
Verify health, authentication, authorization, objects, and reconciliation before resuming workers.
Disable maintenance mode only after an operator records the rollback result.

costBoundary.rule: 14G must stop before apply if the reviewed fixed monthly plan exceeds USD 70 or any variable charge lacks an owner. The existing USD 20 alert is an early warning, not a spending cap.

retentionDecision.vpc: Retain fra1-default outside Terraform state indefinitely as the regional default VPC.
retentionDecision.sharedResources: After promotion, retain the approved app, database cluster, and private bucket for synthetic shared development while a named owner completes a cost and access review every 30 days.
retentionDecision.lapse: If the review, owner, or cost evidence lapses, enable maintenance mode and stop workers. Do not destroy resources automatically.
retentionDecision.destruction: Destroy only exact named resources with fresh owner approval and retained Terraform state.

goldenCases.expectation: An unapproved plan cannot create a resource, state file, credential, or public route.
The project, app, cluster, databases, bucket, components, region, and VPC match the contract exactly.
Terraform reads fra1-default by exact identity, creates no replacement VPC, and binds the app and database privately.
The private bucket rejects public access, enables versioning, and cannot use force_destroy.
Only the provider default address is accepted; custom domains, wildcard CORS, and wildcard callbacks fail validation.
Fixed component counts and sizes total USD 65.15 per month, and a plan over USD 70 fails before apply.
Migration, API, expiry, scanner, reconciler, and Keycloak use separate login roles and denied cross-role operations.
API, scanner, reconciler, and backup operations receive only their declared bucket actions.
No password, token, connection string, object secret, signing key, or private setting reaches the React build or bytes.
Keycloak bootstrap access is removed after MFA enrollment, and a fresh password-only administrator login fails.
Credential rotation has an explicit owner, bounded overlap, verification, revocation, and rollback record without exposing values.
Every operator role has a named MFA account and backup custodian before apply; missing ownership blocks provisioning.
One manifest binds the full commit, image, frontend, lock, Terraform, app spec, and schema digests.
The pre-deploy job reaches e8a1c3f5b7d9, a second run is a no-op, and incompatible services stay blocked.
API, Keycloak, web, migration, expiry, scanner, and reconciler each satisfy their exact health or completion rule.
One scanner instance claims one row at a time with a 15-minute lease, eight attempts, and the fixed retry schedule.
One reconciler instance claims one operation at a time and stale leases recover without duplicate object mutation.
Two expiry invocations for the same scope and business date produce one result through the advisory lock.
Every long-running component stops accepting claims, finishes or releases its current lease, and exits inside the termination window.
A branch push or mutable tag cannot deploy any component automatically.
Logs and evidence contain no token, password, connection string, private key, object secret, signed URL, or document content.
Every contract signal has one owner, severity, threshold, response, retention period, and test method.
A stale heartbeat, old queue item, expired lease, retry, and terminal failure each produce the assigned safe signal.
A forecast or reviewed plan above USD 70 blocks new work; an alert alone never claims spending is capped.
Maintenance mode, owner notification, evidence preservation, rollback selection, and recovery steps have timestamps and named operators.
Both databases restore into isolated targets with the exact schema head and matching identity, row, and signing-key evidence.
Private object restore reproduces exact version, key, count, byte, and digest manifests without public access.
Restored application writes and workers stay disabled until database, identity, object, reconciliation, and artifact checks pass.
Rollback selects the prior schema-compatible manifest and never performs an automatic schema downgrade.
Cleanup deletes only the named isolated recovery targets after sanitized evidence is retained.
A fresh read-only check resolves the exact account, project, VPC, resources, prices, alert, GitHub access, owners, and credential custody.
Phase authorization alone cannot approve a paid apply; the exact settled manifest and cost require dated owner approval.
The first apply and every incompatible update remain in maintenance until every promotion item passes.
Restart and redeploy preserve database, signing keys, objects, scanner, reconciler, expiry, and release identities.
A lapsed 30-day review enables maintenance and stops workers but never destroys the shared resources automatically.
Every inventory and golden-case ID appears once in the independent evidence trace with no owner gap or overlap.
No real data, custom domain, external delivery, automatic deployment, Azure work, retained archive change, or unapproved resource enters Phase 14.
Phase rollback follows 14H, 14G, 14F, 14E, 14D, 14C, 14B, then 14A without deleting preserved resources.
